traceability.notes: Performance data extracted by claude-sonnet-5 reading the PDF directly (native document input), used as a fallback because the deterministic pdfplumber pipeline (summary_report_parser.py) found no per-category breakdown in this report. Model's own extraction notes: This is a qualitative (detection) method study (CSD method for Cronobacter spp. detection). The primary "All samples" row (55/123/24/23 -> SEalt 77.5%, SEref 76.5%, RT 79.1%, FPR 0.0%) is a summary/total across the two categories and was excluded per instructions. Within category 1, sub-tables further split by test portion size (Up to 50 g vs 50-375 g) and by product type (a/b/c: without probiotics, with probiotics, ingredients) exist in Table 4, but only the category-level Total rows (per test portion) were recorded, matching the level of granularity used in the report's own Table 5 summary. The inter-laboratory (collaborative study) section (Section 4) presents a separate, single-level (Level 1) sensitivity/RT/FPR calculation (SEalt=62.5%, SEref=68.8%, RT=50.9%, FPR=0.0%) that is not broken down by food category, so it was not included as a category entry; it is a different study phase (inter-lab reproducibility) rather than the main method-comparison-by-category study reported in Section 3.1. No explicit numeric 'Acceptability Limit' in log units applies since this is qualitative; instead an AL of 2.5 is used for the unpaired RLOD acceptability criterion (not a bias/log AL, so omitted from qualitative schema).
